---
title: "paVerse: From a Messy HRIS Export to a Standardized Attrition Report"
subtitle: "A reference pipeline built on `padm`, `pa.synthetic`, `workforce`, and `attrition`"
date: today
---

```{r setup}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(pa.synthetic)
library(workforce)
library(attrition)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

source("standardize.R")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))
```

## Why this exists

Every pharma company runs `admiral` on the same CDISC data model and gets interoperable analysis
pipelines for free. Every HR analytics team reinvents headcount, tenure, and turnover logic from
scratch — usually with a different, unstated denominator for "turnover rate" every time. This
report is a runnable proof that the same trick pharmaverse plays works here: one shared data model
(`padm`), pure derivation functions built on it (`workforce`), and standardized metrics on top
(`attrition`), all validated against synthetic data with a documented reconciliation invariant.

Nothing in this report is real HR data. `pa.synthetic` generates a seeded, reproducible synthetic
organization — including a deliberately messy raw export and a documented, deliberate
adverse-impact signal in one job family, so downstream fairness tooling has something real to
find later.

## 1. Ingest: a messy vendor export

Real HRIS exports are never `padm`-shaped. `pa.synthetic::pa_synth_raw()` takes a clean event
stream and re-renders it the way a Workday extract actually arrives: renamed columns, three
different date formats mixed row by row, inconsistent casing on the event reason text, and stray
padding whitespace. No information is lost — every quirk is a format problem, not a data-quality
problem — but it has to be handled before anything downstream can trust it.

```{r ingest}
raw <- padm_demo_raw
glimpse_cols <- c("Worker ID", "Effective Date", "Event Reason", "Supervisory Org", "FTE %")
raw[1:8, glimpse_cols] |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Raw export (first 8 rows, subset of columns)") |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(font = "monospace"), locations = cells_body())
```

Three date formats and three casing styles appear in just the first few rows — that's the point.

## 2. Standardize to `padm`

`demo/standardize.R` parses the three date formats, normalizes the event-reason text back to the
controlled vocabulary in `spec/padm/vocab/event-types.csv`, converts `"100%"` strings to numeric
`fte`, and maps vendor column names to `padm` names. This is the one piece of code in this whole
pipeline that's specific to "Workday" as a source system — everything after this line only ever
sees `pa_event`.

```{r standardize}
event <- standardize_workday(raw)

event[1:8, c("person_id", "event_date", "event_type", "event_subtype", "org_unit_id", "fte")] |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Standardized pa_event (same 8 rows)")
```

## 3. Validate against `padm`

`padm_validate()` checks required tables, required columns at the requested conformance level, the
controlled vocabulary, and the two conditional rules in the `pa_event` schema (`event_subtype`
required on `exit`; `base_pay_currency` required whenever `base_pay_amount` is present). The org
and job catalogs are supplied separately from the events extract, as they would be in a real
integration.

```{r validate}
tables <- list(
  pa_person = padm_demo_person,
  pa_event = event,
  pa_org_unit = padm_demo_org_unit,
  pa_job = padm_demo_job
)
validation <- padm_validate(tables, level = "extended")
validation
```

```{r validate-check}
#| echo: false
if (!validation$ok) stop("padm_validate() failed -- the standardized export doesn't conform")
```

Conformance achieved: **`r validation$achieved_level`**. No failures.

## 4. Derive assignments

`wf_assignments()` folds the event stream into `pa_assignment`: one row per person per
uninterrupted assignment interval, SCD-2 style. This is the only place in the pipeline where
"who was where, doing what job, reporting to whom, for how long" gets materialized — and it's a
pure function of `pa_event`, so it can always be rebuilt.

```{r assignments}
assignments <- wf_assignments(event)
cat(sprintf(
  "%s assignment intervals across %s persons (%.1f intervals/person on average)\n",
  format(nrow(assignments), big.mark = ","),
  format(length(unique(assignments$person_id)), big.mark = ","),
  nrow(assignments) / length(unique(assignments$person_id))
))
```

## 5. Headcount and the reconciliation invariant

`wf_snapshot()` produces a dense person-by-month grid; `wf_reconcile()` checks the one invariant
that matters — `opening + hires − exits == closing` — for every period. Because `pa_assignment`
and `pa_headcount_snapshot` are both derived from the same `pa_event` stream, this can only fail if
the derivation logic itself has a bug, never because two independently-maintained tables drifted
apart.

```{r reconcile}
snapshot <- wf_snapshot(assignments, period = "month")
reconcile <- wf_reconcile(snapshot, event, period = "month")

checked <- reconcile$reconciled[!is.na(reconcile$reconciled)]
cat(sprintf("%d / %d monthly periods reconciled exactly\n", sum(checked), length(checked)))
if (!all(checked)) stop("reconciliation invariant failed")

reconcile |>
  tail(12) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Reconciliation, last 12 months") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(opening, hires, exits, expected_closing, closing)) |>
  cols_label(reconciled = "opening + hires − exits == closing")
```

```{r headcount-plot}
#| fig-cap: "Total headcount by month, derived entirely from pa_event"
reconcile |>
  ggplot(aes(period, closing)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2c3e50", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Headcount")
```

## 6. Turnover rate under three definitions — the punchline

This is the sharpest concrete argument for a shared standard: computed on the **identical**
assignments and events, over the **identical** twelve-month window, "turnover rate" produces three
different numbers depending on an unstated denominator choice. `padm` makes `exposure` the
canonical default (`spec/padm/padm-v0.md` §7) precisely because it is the only one that is
mathematically consistent with the event-sourced spine — but `attr_rate()` requires the definition
be named explicitly every time, so a reported number is never ambiguous about what it measures.

```{r turnover}
win_from <- as.Date("2025-01-01")
win_to <- as.Date("2026-01-01")

rates <- bind_rows(lapply(
  c("exposure", "avg_headcount", "beginning_headcount"),
  function(d) attr_rate(assignments, event, win_from, win_to, definition = d)
))

rates |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Calendar-year 2025 turnover, three ways") |>
  fmt_number(columns = denominator, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = rate, decimals = 1) |>
  cols_label(
    definition = "Denominator definition", exits = "Exits",
    denominator = "Denominator", rate = "Turnover rate"
  )
```

```{r rolling}
#| fig-cap: "Trailing 12-month exposure-based turnover rate, monthly"
period_ends <- seq(as.Date("2021-01-31"), as.Date("2025-12-31"), by = "month")
rolling <- attr_rate_rolling(assignments, event, period_ends, window_months = 12, definition = "exposure")

rolling |>
  ggplot(aes(to, rate)) +
  geom_line(color = "#c0392b", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Trailing 12-month turnover (exposure)")
```

## 7. Retention curves by hire cohort

A single point-in-time rate can't answer "are recent hires retaining better or worse than people
hired three years ago at the same point in their tenure?" A Kaplan-Meier curve, grouped by
hire-year cohort, can.

```{r curve}
#| fig-cap: "Kaplan-Meier retention by hire-year cohort, censored at 36 months"
tenure <- wf_tenure(assignments, as_of = win_to - 1)
curve <- attr_curve(tenure, cohort = "hire_year", max_months = 36)

curve |>
  ggplot(aes(time_months, survival, color = group)) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Tenure (months)", y = "Retained", color = "Hire year")
```

## 8. Cohort retention table

The table form of the same idea: fraction of each cohort retained to fixed tenure checkpoints,
correctly excluding people who haven't had the chance to reach a checkpoint yet rather than
counting them as churn.

```{r cohort-table}
attr_cohort(tenure, checkpoints_months = c(3, 6, 12, 24)) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "cohort") |>
  tab_header(title = "Retention by hire-year cohort") |>
  fmt_percent(columns = retention, decimals = 0) |>
  sub_missing(columns = retention, missing_text = "n/a (nobody observable yet)") |>
  cols_label(checkpoint_months = "Tenure checkpoint (months)", n = "Cohort size",
             n_observable = "Observable", retention = "Retained")
```

## 9. Org-unit breakdown, with small-cell suppression

`spec/padm/padm-v0.md` §5 tags every column with a sensitivity tier so a future `pa.privacy`
package can enforce suppression automatically. There's no such package yet, but the reporting
discipline it's meant to enforce is cheap to apply by hand today: any org unit too small to report
on without risking re-identification is suppressed rather than shown.

```{r org-breakdown}
org_lookup <- unique(padm_demo_org_unit[, c("org_unit_id", "org_unit_name")])
units <- unique(assignments$org_unit_id)

by_unit <- bind_rows(lapply(units, function(u) {
  asn_u <- assignments[assignments$org_unit_id == u, ]
  ev_u <- event[event$org_unit_id == u, ]
  size <- attr_rate(asn_u, ev_u, win_from, win_to, "avg_headcount")$denominator
  exp <- attr_rate(asn_u, ev_u, win_from, win_to, "exposure")
  data.frame(org_unit_id = u, avg_headcount = size, exits = exp$exits, rate = exp$rate)
}))

SUPPRESSION_THRESHOLD <- 11 # common small-cell suppression convention

by_unit |>
  left_join(org_lookup, by = "org_unit_id") |>
  mutate(
    suppressed = avg_headcount < SUPPRESSION_THRESHOLD,
    exits = ifelse(suppressed, NA_integer_, exits),
    rate = ifelse(suppressed, NA_real_, rate)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(avg_headcount)) |>
  select(org_unit_name, avg_headcount, exits, rate) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "2025 turnover (exposure) by org unit",
             subtitle = sprintf("Units with average headcount below %d are suppressed", SUPPRESSION_THRESHOLD)) |>
  fmt_number(columns = avg_headcount, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = rate, decimals = 1) |>
  sub_missing(columns = c(exits, rate), missing_text = "suppressed") |>
  cols_label(org_unit_name = "Org unit", avg_headcount = "Avg. headcount",
             exits = "Exits", rate = "Turnover rate")
```

## Reproducibility

Everything above is generated from `pa.synthetic`'s cached demo dataset (`seed = 42`, 600-person
hiring cohort, 2019–2025). Re-running `quarto render demo/attrition-report.qmd` from a clean
checkout reproduces this document exactly. `demo/run.R` runs the same pipeline headless as a CI
smoke test.

```{r versions}
#| echo: false
sessioninfo::package_info(c("pa.synthetic", "workforce", "attrition"), dependencies = FALSE)
```
